parsed.explanation: Derived from the parent regime first: a hostile national border and document system (assigned-sex passport rules, X markers discontinued for new issues, adjudicators invited to weigh document discrepancies and potential lifetime fraud findings, documented detentions of foreign trans travellers, allied travel advisories), plus documented harm in national custody and official 'radically pro-transgender' threat framing. That tier-1 universal exposure sets a low baseline (~0.35). The division moves it up materially but not fully: it imposes no facility ban, has public-accommodations coverage since 2005–06, a gender-identity hate-crime statute with panic defences abolished, marker changes and an X option on state documents, and a healthcare shield — all documented operating for visitors, with no local police targeting. But these cannot override the border, passport and federal custody rules every traveller still passes through. Hence just above the parent, well below the independent-protective tier.
